title: A Night in a Sleeping Car
description: Explore overnight rail travel through sleeping spaces, luggage storage, and the people working aboard a passenger train.
cardDescription: Explore overnight rail travel through sleeping spaces, luggage storage, and the people working aboard a passenger train.
subtheme: A Night in a Sleeping Car
focus: A train compartment can contain a seat by day and sleeping accommodation at night. The clues distinguish the space itself from its bedding and the passage connecting rooms.
solvingTip: Use the location described by each clue: beside the window, above a seat, or along the corridor.
words: Sleeping place aboard a train or ship
Railway car fitted with overnight sleeping accommodation
Railway worker traditionally helping passengers with luggage
Passage between seats or compartments in a rail car
Narrow bed that may be arranged above another
Warm covering spread over a train passenger's bed
Soft head support on a sleeping-car bed
Light fabric layer beneath a sleeper's blanket
Small private room aboard some passenger vehicles
Framework above a seat for storing a travel bag
Document authorizing the passenger's rail journey
Fabric screen drawn across a sleeping space
Describing the higher of two stacked sleeping places
Describing the sleeping place beneath another
Glass opening through which a passenger sees the passing countryside

answerNotes.BERTH: A berth is a place to sleep in this scene; the same word can also name a vessel's assigned mooring place.
answerNotes.SLEEPER: Sleeper names a passenger car here, rather than a person sleeping or a timber beneath railway track.
answerNotes.PORTER: Porter describes a passenger-service role; duties and job titles differ among rail operators and periods.
answerNotes.AISLE: An aisle is a passage for moving through the car, distinct from the individual accommodation beside it.
answerNotes.BUNK: A bunk is the bed itself, while berth can describe the assigned sleeping space.

title: Beside a Steam Locomotive
description: Identify the working parts of a preserved steam locomotive through its heat, motion, and familiar railway fittings.
cardDescription: Identify the working parts of a preserved steam locomotive through its heat, motion, and familiar railway fittings.
focus: Steam pressure moves pistons, and connecting mechanisms transfer that motion to the driving wheels. The clues separate the source of heat from the parts transmitting motion.
solvingTip: Look for a container, a moving component, or the place occupied by the crew.
words: Sliding engine part moved by pressurized steam
Locomotive vessel in which water is heated to produce steam
Chamber where fuel burns in a traditional steam locomotive
Separate vehicle carrying a steam locomotive's fuel and water
Engine chamber in which a steam-driven piston moves
Water vapor supplying power to a traditional locomotive
Black fuel burned by many historical railway engines
Steam-powered sounding device used to give a railway signal
Enclosed crew space of a locomotive
Rigid bar connecting moving locomotive parts
Device controlling the passage of steam
Instrument displaying a boiler pressure reading
Round component rolling on a railway rail
Steel running surface supporting a train's wheels

answerNotes.PISTON: A piston moves back and forth inside a cylinder; rods can transfer that motion to the locomotive's wheels.
answerNotes.BOILER: The boiler contains heated water and steam; it is different from the firebox where fuel burns.
answerNotes.FIREBOX: A firebox provides heat, while the boiler transfers that heat to water.
answerNotes.TENDER: A tender carries supplies; some tank locomotives instead carry their water and fuel on the engine itself.
answerNotes.CYLINDER: Cylinder names the chamber, not the sliding piston inside it.

title: A Canal Boat at the Lock
description: Follow a canal boat through a lock chamber using words for water levels, gates, and the narrow towpath beside the canal.
cardDescription: Follow a canal boat through a lock chamber using words for water levels, gates, and the narrow towpath beside the canal.
subtheme: A Canal Boat at the Lock
focus: A lock changes a boat’s elevation by changing the water level inside a chamber. Its gates and water-control openings have different jobs.
solvingTip: Separate the enclosed water space from the barrier at either end and from the path on shore.
words: Enclosed canal chamber used to raise or lower boats between water levels
Controlled opening through which lock water can flow
Canalside path historically used by animals pulling boats
Stout post around which a boat's mooring line can be secured
Enclosed water space between a canal lock's end gates
Large movable barrier closing the end of a canal lock
Artificial waterway used by these slow-moving boats
Height of the water surface within a lock
Flexible line used to hold a boat alongside
Flat-bottomed cargo vessel associated with canals
Forward end of the boat entering a lock
Rear end of a canal boat
To secure a boat at a stopping place
People working together aboard the canal vessel

answerNotes.LOCK: A lock changes the water level around a floating boat, rather than lifting the boat on a solid platform.
answerNotes.SLUICE: A sluice controls water passage; a gate at the chamber's end allows the boat itself to enter or leave.
answerNotes.TOWPATH: A towpath runs beside the waterway; it is not the underwater route taken by the boat.
answerNotes.BOLLARD: A bollard provides a fixed shore fitting, while the line connects the vessel to it.
answerNotes.CHAMBER: The chamber holds the boat as the surrounding water level changes.

title: Crossing on a Passenger Ferry
description: Picture a short ferry crossing through boarding places, deck fittings, and the people and signals associated with the trip.
cardDescription: Picture a short ferry crossing through boarding places, deck fittings, and the people and signals associated with the trip.
focus: A ferry carries people or vehicles across water on a service route. The clues distinguish boarding structures from the boat’s own parts and from its landing destination.
solvingTip: Read whether the clue describes something on land, on the vessel, or used to announce its movement.
words: Vessel carrying passengers or vehicles across a regular water route
Passage or walkway used to board a vessel
Passenger facility at the end or stopping point of a ferry route
Disturbed water trailing behind a moving boat
Horizontal floor surface aboard a ferry
Landing place where a ferry can be secured
Sloping boarding surface used by vehicles on some ferries
Proof of payment checked before a ferry crossing
Loud sounding device used to signal from a vessel
Workers operating and caring for the ferry
Enclosed passenger space aboard the boat
Shore structure projecting over water toward a landing
Land beside the water crossed by a ferry
Regular course followed by a passenger service

answerNotes.FERRY: Ferry describes a transport service and its vessel; it does not specify one particular hull design.
answerNotes.GANGWAY: A gangway connects boarding areas, while the deck is part of the vessel itself.
answerNotes.TERMINAL: A terminal serves travelers on shore; it is different from the dock structure beside the vessel.
answerNotes.WAKE: A wake forms as a vessel moves through water and differs from the ordinary wind-driven waves around it.
answerNotes.DECK: A deck is a structural surface on the vessel; a pier extends from land into the water.

title: A Paddlewheel Riverboat
description: Look around a traditional riverboat through the turning paddlewheel, steering equipment, and riverside landing.
cardDescription: Look around a traditional riverboat through the turning paddlewheel, steering equipment, and riverside landing.
focus: A paddlewheel pushes against water to propel a boat. A sternwheel is mounted at the rear, while sidewheel arrangements place wheels alongside the hull.
solvingTip: Use the position or purpose of a part. The turning propelling device is different from the wheel used for steering.
words: Flat blade on a riverboat's propelling wheel
Paddlewheel mounted at the rear of a vessel
Movable underwater blade used to steer a riverboat
Person guiding a vessel through a waterway
Riverside structure where a boat loads or unloads
Flowing inland waterway traveled by this vessel
Main body of the riverboat below its upper structures
Floor level on which riverboat passengers can stand
Metal sounding device associated with a traditional boat
Upright exhaust structure on an older powered riverboat
Line used to secure the boat at a landing
Circular steering control in the pilot's station
Left side of a vessel when facing forward

answerNotes.PADDLE: Paddle blades push against water as the wheel rotates; they are not the steering rudder.
answerNotes.STERNWHEEL: A sternwheel is at the stern; sidewheel boats place their propelling wheels at the sides.
answerNotes.RUDDER: A rudder influences direction, whereas a paddlewheel provides propulsion.
answerNotes.PILOT: A river pilot uses local navigation knowledge; the same word also names an aircraft operator in another setting.
answerNotes.WHARF: A wharf is a landing structure on shore, separate from the boat's deck.
